name: Daouda Yıldız-Fasavalu
location: Kessler Interchange, Meridian 88, near Milwaukee and Damen
description:
Daouda is built wide and compact, the kind of body that came from years of adolescent labor before it settled into something functional and calm. His complexion is a warm chestnut brown, his hair worn in tight, close-cut coils shot through with bioluminescent blue threading — a cheap genemod he got at a Mexicantown Libre parlor for his twenty-fifth birthday that he's maintained ever since because his daughter said it made him look like a hero. He has the patient, half-attentive expression of someone who has processed thirty thousand faces through a chokepoint and is no longer surprised by the human shape, but his eyes quicken when something actually breaks pattern.

He's not corrupt, which at Kessler Interchange makes him something of an oddity. He takes Φ12 under the table maybe twice a year when someone's biometric is glitching and they're going to miss a hospital appointment, and he has decided that this is what his moral flexibility budget allows. He has a small shrine to the Interchange E.L.F. — locally called 'the Turnstile' — affixed to the inside of his booth, decorated with expired transit tokens and a photo of his daughter printed on glossy plastic. He believes the Turnstile has kept three serious incidents off his shift in three years, and he's probably right that something has.

core_fears: His daughter inheriting his tier, his ceiling
Making a call that gets someone killed — either through action or inaction
core_desires: Stability that doesn't require constant vigilance to maintain
His daughter going to a Tessera-accredited school
coping_mechanisms: Routine as dignity — doing the small job well as self-respect
Talking to the Turnstile E.L.F. during quiet stretches
blind_spots: Underestimates how much Ferrogate depends on his not asking questions about cargo shipments on the overnight freight rail
psychology.secret: He's been quietly keeping a log of the freight manifests that don't add up — container weights that don't match declared goods, routing anomalies — not because he intends to do anything with it, but because he can't make himself stop noticing.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Warm, straightforward, laced with Malian-Samoan idioms that come out when he's comfortable. Work-mode voice is neutral and procedural.
speech_patterns.cadence: Easy rhythm in personal conversation. Clipped and efficient at the checkpoint.
verbal_tics: Taps his booth wall twice when he approves a crossing — habit, not signal
example_lines: 'I'm going to need you to hold still for the scan, friend. Takes three seconds, then you're on your way.'
'The Turnstile's been quiet today. That's either very good or it's saving something up.'

story_hooks: He's noticed a specific cargo container come through Kessler on a routing that doesn't exist in Ferrogate's official network — three times in two months — and is beginning to feel like his silence about it has made him complicit in something.

His daughter was on a train that experienced a mysterious 'signal fault' that stopped it in the tunnel for two hours; Ferrogate's official explanation doesn't match what Daouda observed on his own terminal that night.
narrative_function: Local color and access point — he controls who moves through Kessler Interchange; information source about transit patterns and irregular commuter behavior; potential ally who can look the other way or flag someone's transit profile; humanizing portrait of low-tier security work.
augmentations: Standard Ferrogate-issue biometric scanner integrated into his right palm (reads heat signatures, ID chips, contraband metabolic markers); bioluminescent blue threading in hair (cosmetic genemod). No combat chrome.
daily_life: Twelve-hour shifts at Booth 7, Kessler Interchange, processing four to six thousand commuters; he brings a thermos of strong sorghum tea and a physical novel he reads in three-minute windows between surges; picks his daughter up from her afterschool program on days he ends shift before 18:00.

decision_rules: Keep the line moving — delay is its own kind of harm
Give people the benefit of the doubt until the scanner says otherwise
escalation_ladder: Firm, louder procedural request with hand signal for backup
Locks the booth gate and calls Transit Response — he is not paid to fight

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm, makes brief eye contact, treats everyone like they're probably having a hard day
interpersonal_modes.friends: Relaxed, genuinely funny, will talk for twenty minutes about his daughter's drawings if you let him

stress_responses.medium: Focuses entirely on procedure — every step by the book
stress_responses.high: Shuts down personal conversation entirely, goes mechanical, prays quietly to the Turnstile during his break

contradictions: Believes the system is basically fair while privately cataloguing evidence that it isn't
habits: Leaves an expired transit token at his E.L.F. shrine every Sunday
Reads the last page of a novel before starting it — he likes knowing something survives
breaking_points: His daughter is endangered as a direct result of something moving through his checkpoint

timeline.event: Age 19: Joined Ferrogate Transit Security as a platform attendant
Age 24: Promoted to checkpoint operator after commendation for diffusing a platform altercation without injury
Age 26: Daughter Amara born; mother not in the picture
Age 29: Started the unofficial freight manifest log
Age 31: Currently at Booth 7, Kessler Interchange, three years running
